trust_decision.summary: Front-end user password storage and verification: register stores an unsalted MD5 hex digest (salt hard-coded to "0") and login authenticates by string-equality against a fresh unsalted MD5 of the supplied password, both in UserServiceImpl.

landing_point.why: The only DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex call sites in the Java tree are in this class (import at line 30); a grep for MD5 lands here directly.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: No second password hasher at the pinned commit: SysUser has a password field (src/main/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/dao/entity/SysUser.java:92-97) but no admin login/register code exists; /admin/login is only an interceptor exclusion (src/main/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/core/config/WebConfig.java:57). Author registration (src/main/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/controller/author/AuthorController.java:48-51) handles no password.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered route exists to dismiss. The only argument available is the legacy-hash path: a solver could keep accepting stored unsalted MD5 hashes forever, without rehashing on successful login, 'for backward compatibility'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing accounts whose stored password is a legacy 32-hex unsalted MD5 must still be able to log in (with transparent upgrade). A fix that only accepts BCrypt locks out every existing user, and a fix that keeps the MD5 comparison as an unconditional fallback leaves weak hashes in place.

O6_input_shapes: login against a BCrypt-format stored hash
login against a legacy MD5-format stored hash (inferred from c_same_check_name=isBCryptHash at 2 sites; diff body not available)

O7_producer.where: Hash produced inline in the service: src/main/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/service/impl/UserServiceImpl.java:72. No PasswordEncoder bean exists (only a SecurityFilterChain for actuator, src/main/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/NovelApplication.java:56-63). The user_info DDL (password column width) is not in this repository.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A password-change field in updateUserInfo / UserInfoUptReqDto that re-hashes with MD5
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The profile-update endpoint already writes UserInfo fields. A maintainer adding 'change password' would copy the register code's MD5 line.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An admin login (/admin/login, already excluded in WebConfig.java:57) that verifies the SysUser password with its own MD5 compare in a separate admin service package
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sys_user entity and mapper exist and the route is already whitelisted, so a second implementation in another package is the most realistic distant sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A password-reset/forgot-password flow in the manager layer that writes a new hash directly via UserInfoMapper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Verify-code and mail-sender infrastructure (RegisterMailSender) already exist for exactly this kind of flow.

O10_build.project_tests: None for this area. src/test holds only a MyBatis-Plus code generator (src/test/java/io/github/xxyopen/novel/generator/Generator.java).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap md5DigestAsHex for BCrypt in both register and login, which locks out every existing MD5-hashed account (or the opposite: keep an MD5 fallback with no rehash).
